standard_prerequisites.name: The pullback of a sieve along a morphism into a member
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the pullback of a sieve along a morphism that already belongs to it.

core_obligations: Finite intersections (proof lines 11243-11251): the empty intersection is covered by the third axiom, and for two covering sieves the author uses the second axiom, observing that the pullback of one along a morphism belonging to the other is the pullback of the intersection.

Upward closure (proof lines 11254-11258): for a covering sieve contained in another, the pullback of the larger one along a morphism belonging to the smaller is the whole representable sieve by the companion calculation, so it belongs to the topology by the third axiom, and the second axiom then gives the conclusion.
proof_roadmap: Handle the empty intersection by the third axiom.
Use the second axiom and a pullback computation for two covering sieves.
Use the third and second axioms for upward closure.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records two closure properties of the collection of covering sieves of a topology: it is closed under finite intersections and under passing to larger sieves (statement lines 11231-11240). The proof is a complete verification: the empty intersection is handled by the third axiom and the binary case by the second axiom together with the observation that the relevant pullbacks agree (proof lines 11243-11251); upward closure is obtained by computing the pullback of the larger sieve along a morphism belonging to the smaller one and applying the third and second axioms (proof lines 11254-11258). The non-formal content is the two pullback computations. The claim is H1: two short verifications.
